title: Authorize Engine F1-F10 decomposition from the bootstrap capability ledger
description:
Single machine-enforced gate between the bootstrap capability ledger and any
engine decomposition work. bd forbids epic->task dependencies, so eshyra-olc5
itself cannot depend on eshyra-o9bd.19.5.1; this task carries that dependency on
the epic's behalf, and the ten per-family decomposition tasks depend on this one.
The Engine F* epics will still appear in bd ready — that is a bd display
limitation, not permission to start. All executable work below them is blocked
here.

Authorize decomposition only when ALL of the following hold:

  1. The bootstrap ledger (eshyra-o9bd.19.5.1) exists and is labelled
     non-authoritative.
  2. Every capability membership has a GENERATED query, not a hand-copied count.
  3. The eshyra-2n1t reconciliation is complete: every bead of that closed epic
     classified as different scope/taxonomy | stale readiness mapping |
     incomplete integration | premature closure.
  4. Each capability is classified into reusable implementation primitives, with
     cross-family primitives named once and assigned an owning family.
  5. Each Engine F epic has a proposed child decomposition recorded on its
     decomposition task.
  6. No implementation child anywhere is derived from copied hook counts alone.

COUNT HYGIENE: every number here is a SNAPSHOT. The generated ledger/predicate
is authoritative. No acceptance test may require a hand-copied number (e.g.
391, 399, 77, 79).

*** engine:F* IS A QUALIFIED PREFIX. engine:F1..F10 are the pack's
executionReadiness engineHooks families — NOT the CLOSED epic eshyra-2n1t's
different F1-F10, and NOT the fable:F1..F8 audit findings.
acceptance_criteria:
• All six authorization conditions above are satisfied and evidenced.
• Every engine:F* family has a generated membership query committed and runnable.
• The eshyra-2n1t four-way classification artifact is linked and complete.
• Cross-family primitives are enumerated with a single owning family each.
• No implementation children exist yet anywhere under eshyra-olc5.
